purpose: Transform one video concept into viewer-owned tools without turning the channel into therapy, doctrine or authority.

daily_invitation.frame: A feeling can be real while its forecast is still being tested.
daily_invitation.question: What is your body forecasting today—and what evidence is it using?
daily_invitation.landing: Notice the chair, your feet and one fact in the room before answering.

belief_examiner.title: The Three-Part Forecast Check
belief_examiner.instructions: Write one sentence in each field. Do not argue with the feeling or force a new one.

fields.name: Sensation
fields.prompt: What can you directly notice in the body without naming the emotion?
fields.example: My chest is tight and my breathing is shallow.

fields.name: Prediction
fields.prompt: What event or outcome is the mind forecasting?

fields.name: Present evidence
fields.prompt: What is verifiably happening right now?
fields.example: I am sitting in a room. The conversation has not started.

fields.name: Revision condition
fields.prompt: What new evidence would make the forecast stronger, weaker or different?
fields.example: The other person’s actual words and actions.

belief_examiner.boundary: This is a reflection exercise, not diagnosis or treatment. Persistent, severe or concerning symptoms deserve appropriate professional attention.

conversation_prompt.question: When you say something feels wrong, which part is bodily sensation, which part is prediction, and which part is already known?
conversation_prompt.use: Ask with curiosity, not as a way to dismiss another person’s feeling or override their boundaries.

grounding_audio.title: Before the Forecast Becomes the Weather
grounding_audio.voice: Liam, slow and warm, no mystical certainty
grounding_audio.script: Let the feeling be here without asking it to leave. Notice where it touches the body: pressure, warmth, movement, stillness. Name only what you can observe. Now notice the forecast attached to it. What does the mind believe is about to happen? You do not have to accept or reject that prediction yet. Feel the chair beneath you. Notice both feet. Look for one ordinary object in the room. Let one breath arrive without turning it into a test. The sensation is present. The prediction is a possibility. The room is also present. What changes when all three are allowed to be visible at once?
grounding_audio.boundary: A non-clinical grounding and reflection practice; not treatment or crisis support.

community_prompt.prompt: Without sharing anything too private, describe a time when the same bodily signal received two different labels—such as anxiety and excitement. What changed the forecast?
moderation: Do not tell anyone their feeling is unreal.
Distinguish personal experience from universal claims.

educator_card.activity: Give students a neutral scenario and ask them to separate bodily observation, predicted outcome and available evidence.
educator_card.learning_goal: Practice revisable inference without implying that emotion is fake or irrational.
educator_card.discussion_question: How can two people receive similar signals but construct different interpretations?
educator_card.boundary: Use age-appropriate examples; avoid asking students to disclose mental-health experiences.

success_signals: A viewer reports trying the three-part check.
A viewer distinguishes bodily sensation from forecast without dismissing either.
A viewer offers a thoughtful disagreement or alternative interpretation.
A viewer asks what evidence would revise the prediction.
risk_signals: A viewer concludes that anxiety or emotion is imaginary.
A viewer treats the practice as medical advice.
A viewer blames themselves for not changing a feeling.
A viewer transfers certainty to the channel rather than testing the idea.
